learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes; a missed fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: read the ring pattern
items.prompt: A six-membered conjugated ring has two opposite carbonyl groups. Which redox form does this head-group pattern support?
options: The fully reduced hydroquinone form
The oxidized quinone form
A saturated hydrocarbon tail
A phosphate ester
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: balance reduction
items.prompt: Which net equation represents reduction of quinone Q to hydroquinone QH2?
options: Q + O2 → QH2
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: classify the ring change
items.prompt: A carrier's ring changes from two hydroxyl groups to two carbonyl groups. What net process occurred at the head group?
options: Reduction with uptake of 2 e− and 2 H+
Hydrolysis of the isoprenoid tail
Oxidation with release of 2 e− and 2 H+
Phosphorylation of both oxygens
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: locate redox function
items.prompt: Which region of ubiquinone directly changes between the fully oxidized and fully reduced forms?
options: The quinone ring oxygen groups
Every carbon in the isoprenoid tail
A peptide backbone attached to the ring
A phosphate group on the terminal tail carbon
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: evaluate carrier R
items.prompt: Carrier R has an unchanged hydrophobic tail and a ring bearing two hydroxyl groups instead of two carbonyls. Which combined statement is supported?
options: R is oxidized after net release of 2 e− and 2 H+
R is reduced after net uptake of 2 e− and 2 H+
R is reduced because its tail gained two carbon atoms
R is oxidized because ring hydroxyls release electrons
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: compare two structural variants
items.prompt: Variant A replaces one quinone carbonyl oxygen with a non-redox-active group while preserving the tail. Variant B shortens the hydrophobic tail while preserving both quinone carbonyls. Which paired prediction is best supported?
options: A weakens head-group redox; B weakens membrane retention
A weakens membrane retention; B weakens head-group redox
A preserves head-group redox; B preserves membrane retention
A strengthens head-group redox; B strengthens membrane retention
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: carbonyl versus hydroxyl
items.prompt: Which structural change marks net reduction in the Q/QH2 pair?
options: Two ring hydroxyls become two carbonyls
The tail loses all double bonds
Two ring carbonyls become two hydroxyls
The ring is cleaved into two fragments
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: carrier S
items.prompt: Carrier S begins with two ring carbonyls and accepts 2 e− and 2 H+ while its tail remains unchanged. What product pattern is expected?
options: A ring with two hydroxyl groups
A ring with four carbonyl groups
A tail with two phosphate groups
Complete loss of the ring oxygens
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: assign region to function
items.prompt: Which head–tail function map is supported for ubiquinone?
options: Head—membrane anchoring; tail—carbonyl redox conversion
Head—carbonyl redox conversion; tail—membrane anchoring
Head—peptide synthesis; tail—nuclear-envelope transport
Head—DNA sequence binding; tail—phosphate-group transfer
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: evaluate analog C
items.prompt: Analog C keeps a long hydrophobic tail but replaces both head-group carbonyls with groups that cannot undergo the Q/QH2 conversion. Which outcome is most direct?
options: Membrane residence may remain; head-group redox fails
The analog must become water soluble because the tail remains hydrophobic
The analog performs normal redox chemistry because localization alone is sufficient
The analog automatically carries four electrons instead of two
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
